observationsNotFindings: STALE CROSS-ROW CITATION — the most substantive item in this review, and I traced it fully before deciding. basedOn.signedIndexJoinV2 cites signed-index-leftover-join.v2 (frozen at HEAD 5d5d778 / required-now 26) as the DR-112 ROW join and sources the standing 'OBL-G08-FX-AUTHORING and OBL-RESERVED-NUMBERS remain leftover-design on that row' to it. But signed-index-leftover-join.v3 was ADOPTED at D-187's predecessor D-178 as the current DR-112 leftover remasurement, at HEAD afb115d / required-now 28. The subject never mentions v3, D-178, or v3's digest. There is also an internal asymmetry worth naming: this artifact's own predecessorV2.role declares a v2 measured at 5d5d778/26 'not recordable as a current leftover remasurement because file 08 moved and required-now is 28', yet it relies on a different join's v2, measured at that same stale point, for a live standing. NOT A FINDING, for four reasons. First, the substantive claim is TRUE either way: I checked both, and signed-index v2 and v3 carry an identical leftoverDesign set {OBL-G08-FX-AUTHORING, OBL-RESERVED-NUMBERS}, so the conclusion the subject draws is unchanged. Second, nothing is closed, licensed, or SATISFIED on the basis of the citation — OBL-RESERVED-NUMBERS-NOT-STOLEN is leftoverDesign false and its entire purpose is to NOT take the obligation. Third, the pinned digest 38bdb3a0 genuinely is signed-index v2's current digest, so no custody claim is false. Fourth, the block and reason are byte-identical to the ACCEPTed g08-leftover-join.v2 and outside this successor's stated scope. COORDINATOR NOTE: this is stale rather than wrong today, but it becomes substantively wrong the moment a future signed-index successor changes that leftover set. Worth refreshing to v3 / D-178 whenever this obligation is next legitimately in scope.

PURPOSE CLAUSE WITHOUT AN ANTECEDENT, third occurrence. purpose says 'Replace predecessor self-version closing sentence with the generic form', but no version in this chain ever contained a 'This vN' sentence — v1, v2, and v3 all scan clean, and v2's predecessor.role already used the generic 'Predecessor roles do not claim the successor version number'. Updated wave tally now that this artifact exists: eleven leftover-joins carry the identical clause, and three had nothing to replace — anti-lockstep v2, provider v3, and this one. Not a finding: the clause describes provenance of an edit rather than a measured property, and the property it names holds. Worth trimming from the template where it does not apply.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Seventeen attacks run, seventeen refuted. The subject is a genuine remeasurement of frozen v2 onto live HEAD 5ba5d16 / file 08 f909ddff / required-now 28, and the prompt's explicit token requirement is met — file08StatusToken is OPEN, byte-equal to the live DR-G08 status column. The four corpus classes are corroborated across four sources including the live register. ONE ITEM FOR ATTENTION, logged as an observation: the subject cites signed-index-leftover-join.v2 as the DR-112 row join, but v3 of that join was adopted at D-178 and is the current remasurement; the subject never mentions v3 or D-178. It does not sustain as a finding because both versions carry an identical leftover set, so the claim is true either way, nothing is licensed by it, the pinned digest is genuine, and the block is byte-carried from the ACCEPTed v2. But it is stale rather than wrong only for as long as that set stays identical, and there is an internal asymmetry — this artifact calls its own 5d5d778/26 predecessor non-current while relying on another join's 5d5d778/26 version for a live standing. Worth refreshing to v3 / D-178 when that obligation is next in scope.
